title: City money to the school district and City College
question: How much does the City hand to the school district and City College each year, and can a reader follow it in the City's open ledger?
finding: The Controller reports that in fiscal 2025 the City's education enrichment fund contributed $96.3 million to the school district, a second voter-approved fund $35.0 million and a parcel tax for educators' pay $54.0 million: about $3,268 per pupil. The City's open vendor ledger for the same year shows $15.0 million paid to the district under its name, and the district reported $27.0 million from cities and counties to the federal survey for fiscal 2024: the main transfers cannot be followed in either. City departments paid City College $27.4 million in fiscal 2020 and $12.2 million in fiscal 2025, mostly from the children's department, whose Free City College programme the Controller audits; a further $326 million shown against the college's name in fiscal 2025 is coded to a department and fund named for the college district itself, and appears to be the college's own money passing through the City treasury.
how: Three records are set side by side. (1) The City's vendor-payment ledger, fiscal 2017 on: everything paid to the district and to City College under their names, by department; payments coded to the department and fund named for the college district itself are shown apart. (2) The City ledger's "Public Education Fund (Prop H)" grant line in the children's department, which exists only for fiscal 2015 to 2017. (3) What City budget documents say: the Controller's nine-month report for 2025-26 (table of baselines and set-asides: actual for 2024-25, budget for 2025-26) and the Mayor's 2019 budget book. The district's own report of money from cities and counties to the federal survey is shown beside them.
limits: The enrichment fund and the student success fund were created by measures San Francisco voters approved (in 2004 and 2022, according to the Mayor's budget books); the Controller's table shows the enrichment fund set as a share of City revenue. The vendor ledger records payments made by voucher to a named payee; a transfer made another way, or a grant line not coded with the payee's name, will not appear, which is the likely reason for the gap, not missing money. The parcel tax is a tax earmarked for educators' pay that the Controller lists beside the City's contributions; whether to call it City money is a matter of definition. Figures from budget documents are for single years; the year-by-year series of the enrichment fund is in the Controller's annual reports, which are not on disk.
